nodes.summary: The distribution function is continuous in the mean.
nodes.title: Continuity of the Poisson distribution function in the mean

nodes.summary: The Gamma law of shape `k + 1` and rate `r` (Mathlib's `gammaMeasure`) has upper tail `P(Gamma(k + 1, r) > x) = F_k(r x)`. This is the Erlang tail `gammaMeasure_real_Ioi_natCast_add_one` in `GammaMoments`, rewritten with the definition of `poissonCDF`.
nodes.title: Poisson–Gamma duality

nodes.summary: For every mean `r ≥ 0` and `0 < α < 1`, `P_r(r ≤ u_α(K)) ≥ 1 - α` when `K ~ Poisson(r)`.
nodes.title: Exact coverage of Garwood's bound

nodes.summary: The bound is positive for `0 < α < 1`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the Garwood upper bound

nodes.summary: The bound is strictly increasing in the observed count.
nodes.title: Garwood upper bound is strictly increasing in the count

nodes.summary: After observing `0` the bound is `u_α(0) = log (1 / α)` (`e^{-u} = α`).
nodes.title: Garwood upper bound after observing zero

nodes.summary: Garwood's exact upper confidence bound for a Poisson mean after observing `k`, at level `α`: `u_α(k) = sup {x ≥ 0 | α ≤ F_k(x)}`. For `0 < α < 1` it is the root of `F_k(u) = α` (`poissonCDF_garwoodUpper`).
nodes.title: Garwood's exact upper confidence bound

nodes.summary: The derivative in the mean telescopes: `∂_x F_k(x) = -e^{-x} x^k / (k!)`.
nodes.title: Derivative of the Poisson distribution function in the mean

nodes.summary: A nonnegative mean lies below the bound iff it is not rejected: `x ≤ u_α(k) ↔ α ≤ F_k(x)`.
nodes.title: Means below the Garwood upper bound are exactly the non-rejected ones

nodes.summary: The bound solves `F_k(u_α(k)) = α`.
nodes.title: Garwood upper bound solves the distribution function equation

nodes.summary: The distribution function is strictly increasing in `k` at every positive mean.
nodes.title: Poisson distribution function is strictly increasing in the count

nodes.summary: The distribution function is monotone in `k` at every nonnegative mean.
nodes.title: Poisson distribution function is monotone in the count

nodes.summary: The distribution function is positive at every nonnegative real mean.
nodes.title: Positivity of the Poisson distribution function

nodes.summary: The distribution function is strictly decreasing in the mean on `[0, ∞)`.
nodes.title: Poisson distribution function is strictly decreasing in the mean

nodes.summary: At mean `0` the Poisson law is the point mass at `0`: `F_k(0) = 1`.
nodes.title: Poisson distribution function at mean zero
Poisson distribution function at count zero

nodes.summary: The Poisson distribution function `F_k(x) = ∑_{j ≤ k} e^{-x} x^j / (j!)` as a function of the mean `x` (defined for every real `x`; it is a probability only for `0 ≤ x`).
nodes.title: Poisson distribution function as a function of the mean

nodes.summary: `poissonCDF r k` is the distribution function of Mathlib's `poissonMeasure r` at `k`.
nodes.title: Poisson distribution function agrees with the Poisson law

nodes.summary: For `K ~ Poisson(r)` and every `α ≥ 0`, `P(F_r(K) ≤ α) ≤ α`. (For `α < 0` the event is empty.)
nodes.title: Super-uniformity of the distribution-function transform

nodes.summary: For fixed `k`, `F_k(x) → 0` as the mean `x → ∞`.
nodes.title: Poisson distribution function vanishes as the mean grows

nodes.summary: For a fixed nonnegative mean, `F_k(x) → 1` as `k → ∞`.
nodes.title: Poisson distribution function tends to one as the count grows
